page: Amazon Web Services m5a.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supporting two threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight significant differences between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance falls within the bottom 10%, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 729.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 591.38. Similarly, single-threaded compression benchmarks such as gzip (16.68 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (6.0 GB/sec) remain low. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics scale reliably into the middle 50%, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7086.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 30531.59. The processor demonstrates particular competence in cryptographic operations, achieving a strong PassMark CPU encryption score of 38866.32 due to hardware acceleration.

Memory bandwidth measures 90.8 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 44.98 GB/sec for writes, sustaining middle-tier operational throughput across memory-intensive benchmarks. Redis achieves 29.73 million SET operations per second, while static web serving operates at 16.15 GB/sec. LLM inference shows typical CPU limitations, maintaining 111.36 tokens/sec text generation for small 135M models, but dropping to 6.24 tokens/sec for 7B models.

The m5a.12xlarge presents a cost-effective, high-density CPU core footprint where absolute single-thread speed is secondary. Because it lacks onboard ephemeral storage, data-heavy systems must rely on network-attached storage. This instance suits parallelized general-purpose workloads, mid-tier enterprise application clusters, software compilation pipelines, backend web serving fleets, and distributed data processing frameworks.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.12xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) from an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no integrated local disks and no GPU acceleration. While its single-core compute performance sits in the lower tier—reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 729.0 and slow single-threaded compression speeds—the instance scales effectively across concurrent tasks, delivering a multi-core Geekbench score of 7086.0, a PassMark CPU score of 30531.59, and strong cryptographic acceleration. With an uncached memory read bandwidth of 90.8 GB/sec and 29.73 million Redis SET operations per second, m5a.12xlarge delivers balanced multithreaded capacity suitable for enterprise web serving, backend application runtimes, software compilation, and scalable microservices architectures.
